q37e4475d.question: Which Story-definition document does a Plan-driven standalone Story pin as documents.story? Recommendation: the story role is required only when a DEF exists for the epicHash (an epic Story, where it is the DEF); a standalone Story has none, so its set is lld and plan, and the plan-path identity check uses the Plan artifact id.
q37e4475d.choice: Required document set by the Story's stored artifacts: a Plan exists, then lld and plan, plus story only when a DEF exists for the epicHash; only an LLD exists, then lld; only an ISSUE exists (no LLD, no Plan), then issue; otherwise none. The issue role is never part of the set when a Plan or an LLD exists. The plan-path identity check uses the Plan artifact id, and only when the route has a Plan.
q37e4475d.rationale: User accepted the recommendation with the self-review F2 correction (SELF-REVIEW.md): the issue role applies only to the ISSUE-only route. Also from F1: only the new-request call of prepareReviewPacket (admission.ts:80) takes a route, plumbed from startTaskReview through the coordinator start into admission; resume and publication stay historical with no route, and the LLD's startTaskReview postcondition that says otherwise is superseded.

summary.prose: The code review stops assuming every Story has a Story document, an LLD and a Plan. The daemon reads which of the Story's artifacts exist (ISSUE, LLD, PLAN, BUILD) and requires the review packet to name exactly those documents. A Story with a Plan is reviewed per Plan task exactly as today; a Story without one is reviewed as a single unit derived from its BUILD task against the design record it does have, so the BUILD can be completed by a passing independent whole-story review on every route.

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: Standalone feature — no parent HLD. Design directly against the repo, grounded on the s1 analyze passes. There are no HLD shared contracts to honour.

boundary.internal: Make the code review's documents and review units follow the Story's process flow (ISSUE-a84e610b0a910d49).

dataModelChanges.details: From a required {story, lld, plan} to an object whose keys story, lld, plan and issue are each optional DocumentSchema and no other key is allowed. PacketSchema is cloned from it, so submissions and stored history share the shape. The required set is not in the schema: prepareReviewPacket requires it from the route. Relationship: each document is a pointer {path, commit} to a committed canonical artifact owned by the Story (many documents to one Story; the Story's route fixes which exist). Compatibility: every stored packet has all three of story, lld and plan, so it still decodes, and a stored review summary's scope.documents (a Pick of StoredPacketSchema) and the checkpoint schema follow the same shape.
dataModelChanges.schemaDiff: documents: { story: Document, lld: Document, plan: Document }  ->  documents: { story?: Document, lld?: Document, plan?: Document, issue?: Document }

dataModelChanges.details: A read-only description of the Story's stored artifacts: epicHash, storyId, whether a PLAN, an LLD and an ISSUE record exist under their artifact ids, and the BUILD record's task ids and focus. It is derived in the daemon from planArtifactId, lldArtifactId, issueArtifactId and buildArtifactId read with artifactJsonPath, so the route follows what was actually produced. The required document set is: story, lld and plan when a PLAN exists (an epic or a standalone sized Story); lld alone when only an LLD exists; issue alone when only an ISSUE exists; none when neither exists (trivial). A PLAN with no LLD, or an LLD and a PLAN with an ISSUE, are handled by the same rule: exactly the roles that exist, with story added only when the Plan route has a Story definition.

When the route has no Plan, prepared.tasks holds one PlanTask-shaped unit: id equal to the BUILD's task id (so the completion gate's BUILD-task coverage check holds), order 1, a title and summary taken from the design record (ISSUE title, LLD story title, or BUILD focus), acceptanceChecks taken from that record's stated done conditions (the ISSUE's fix intent; the LLD's acceptance criteria with their proving tests; the BUILD focus for a trivial change), size derived from the number of selected changed files, empty dependsOn and derivedFrom and no planned tests. It is never written to disk; it exists only in the prepared packet.

The check that documents.plan.path ends with PLAN-<epicHash>-<story>.json or /PLAN.md applies only when the route has a Plan; for other routes the equivalent identity is checked in prepareReviewPacket against the document the route requires (the LLD or ISSUE artifact id for this epicHash and story).

errorCases.response: Refuse the start with the message naming the roles required and the roles supplied; nothing is admitted or written
errorCases.userImpact: The controller corrects the packet and calls start again

errorCases.scenario: A required document is not a committed canonical artifact of the right workflow for this epicHash and story
errorCases.detection: The document loader reads the committed blob and its canonical JSON head, then checks meta.workflow (plan, design.story, issue) and, per role, meta.epicHash or meta.issueHash against the route's epicHash and meta.storyId against the story
errorCases.userImpact: The controller pins the right artifact at a commit that contains it

errorCases.scenario: The route has a PLAN record that has no tasks or malformed tasks
errorCases.detection: The existing Plan row validation (tasksEnumerateSchema, validatePlanRows, tasks.length > 0) runs whenever the route has a Plan
errorCases.userImpact: A broken Plan still blocks review, as it should

errorCases.scenario: The Story has no BUILD record, or the BUILD has no task ids
errorCases.detection: startTaskReview reads buildArtifactId for the Story via artifactJsonPath and checks body.tasks before building the route
errorCases.response: Refuse with a message that the BUILD must exist before a review; no derived unit is invented
errorCases.userImpact: The review cannot start before the build has been validated

errorCases.scenario: A route with no Plan whose BUILD has more than one task id
errorCases.detection: The route builder counts BUILD body.tasks
errorCases.response: Refuse: the design derives one unit from a single BUILD task, and a multi-task BUILD without a Plan has no defined units
errorCases.userImpact: Such a BUILD would need a Plan; this cannot arise from the current routes

errorCases.scenario: A stored packet or checkpoint is re-read after the route's artifacts changed (for example a Plan was added later)
errorCases.detection: Resume and publication re-read stored history with historical true and no route, so the stored documents and units are used; admission still compares the saved selected task ids with the prepared ones
errorCases.response: Keep reviewing against the pinned stored documents; a mismatch between saved and prepared task ids is refused as today
errorCases.userImpact: A review started on one route is not silently re-interpreted

errorCases.scenario: The completion gate sees a derived-unit review whose unit id is not the BUILD task id
errorCases.detection: inspectTaskCompletion already requires every BUILD task id among the whole-story review's task ids
errorCases.response: Report the gap 'Whole-story review does not cover every current BUILD task' and withhold completion
errorCases.userImpact: BUILD approval stays withheld until a correct review exists

invariantsToPreserve.text: Everything downstream of prepareReviewPacket consumes prepared.tasks and prepared.packet.documents only, so the units' ids are the only coupling between the packet and the admission, publication and completion checks.
Stored packets, checkpoints and review-summary scopes written before this change must still decode and validate; the documents schema only becomes more permissive.
A Story with a Plan keeps its exact documents, units, task attribution and error messages.
BUILD completion requires a passing whole-story review that covers every BUILD task id and carries the BUILD's fingerprint and reviewer provenance; the derived unit must not weaken any of these.
The route is never taken from the submitted packet; it comes from the Story's stored artifacts, and the daemon chooses the reviewer from the BUILD's author as today.

migration.stateBefore: The review packet requires documents {story, lld, plan} and prepareReviewPacket takes the epicHash and storyId from the Plan, requires every document to belong to the Plan's epic, and derives all review units from the Plan's tasks. A Story whose route produced no Plan (and, for trivial and bugfix routes, no LLD) cannot submit a valid packet, so it can never obtain the passing whole-story review the BUILD completion gate demands (see the analyze bundles on the packet validation, the Plan-task units and the completion gate).
migration.stateAfter: The packet's documents are an object whose story, lld, plan and issue roles are optional in the schema. The daemon reads the Story's stored artifacts to build a route, and prepareReviewPacket requires exactly the roles the route produced. With a Plan the units are the Plan's tasks as before; without a Plan one derived unit carries the BUILD's task id. Stored packets, checkpoints and review records written before the change decode and validate unchanged.

migrationSteps.action: Loosen the stored and submitted packet schemas so each document role is optional and an issue role is allowed, keeping additionalProperties false so no other key is accepted; stored history still decodes because every stored packet has story, lld and plan

Teach prepareReviewPacket to take an optional route, require exactly the route's document roles, keep the existing Plan validation when the route has a Plan, and derive one review unit from the BUILD task when it does not
Have the daemon entry read the Story's PLAN, LLD, ISSUE and BUILD records to build the route on start, resume and publication, and apply the Plan-path identity check only when the route has a Plan
Update the advertised packet schema, the code-review guide and the project instructions that describe the three documents so they describe the route-dependent set
Run the Plan-driven review tests unchanged, then the new route tests, before relying on the new routes for a real BUILD

migration.backwardCompat: The packet schema only becomes more permissive, so every packet a controller sends today (story, lld and plan) is still accepted and validated by the same rules and messages. Stored checkpoints and published code-review records keep their documents and decode as before. A controller on a no-Plan route that previously could not start a review can now start one. A packet that names a document the route did not produce is now refused with a message naming the roles, which is stricter only for Stories that previously could not pass at all.

alternativesConsidered.name: Route-derived document set and a derived single review unit
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: The host works out the Story's route from its stored artifacts, requires exactly the documents that route produced, and for a route without a Plan derives one review unit from the BUILD's task.
alternativesConsidered.approach: The packet's documents become a map of the roles the route produced: story, lld and plan for a Plan-driven Story (unchanged), lld alone for a small feature, issue alone for a small bugfix, none for a trivial change. prepareReviewPacket no longer trusts the submitter on what is required: it reads the Story's stored artifacts (ISSUE, LLD, PLAN, BUILD for the epicHash and storyId) to find the route, then requires the submitted set to equal the set that route produced and each document to be a committed canonical artifact of the right workflow for this story. When there is a Plan its tasks are the units as today. When there is none, prepared.tasks holds one derived unit whose id is the BUILD's task id (s1), whose acceptance checks come from the design record the route has (the LLD's acceptance criteria and test strategy, the ISSUE's fix intent, or the BUILD focus), and whose size is derived from the selected change count. Everything downstream already consumes prepared.tasks and prepared.packet.documents, so it needs no change except the stored shapes, which accept the new keys as optional while old records stay readable.
pros: Smallest change that fully meets the issue: only the packet shape and prepareReviewPacket change, because downstream already iterates prepared.tasks and prepared.packet.documents
The route is read from stored artifacts, so it cannot be claimed falsely to skip a Plan the Story actually has
The completion gate works unchanged, since the derived unit's id is the BUILD's task id
Plan-driven Stories keep exactly today's behaviour and stored records
cons: The stored packet and checkpoint schemas gain optional keys and a new issue role, which is a schema change to persisted history that must remain readable
Reading artifacts to find the route adds a lookup and a new failure mode for an unknown route
One derived unit means a small bugfix gets one assessment, not a finer split, which is right for its size but a design decision to record

alternativesConsidered.name: Explicit route field in the packet, discriminated union
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: The submitter names the route in the packet and the schema is a union of one shape per route.
alternativesConsidered.approach: The packet gains a route field with the values epic-story, feature, small, trivial, bugfix-small and bugfix-sized, and the schema becomes a discriminated union whose members list the exact documents each route requires. The validator dispatches on route, and the route is cross-checked against the BUILD record's sizeClass and standalone flag. Units and the derived unit work as in a1. The MCP and RPC advertise the union.
pros: The contract is explicit in the schema, so a bad packet fails at decode with a precise message
Easy to document in the guide, one shape per route
cons: Duplicates knowledge the stored artifacts already hold, and the submitter can mis-state the route, so a cross-check is needed anyway
A larger union touches the stored schemas, checkpoint, record scope, MCP schema and tests for every route
Every new route in triage means a new union member, which recreates the hardcoding this Story removes
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Works but recreates a route enumeration in the schema and duplicates what the stored artifacts already say.

alternativesConsidered.name: Generate a minimal Plan for routes without one
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Keep the triple but have the build step write a one-task Plan and, where missing, an LLD stub so the review always finds them.
alternativesConsidered.approach: The build stage writes a canonical one-task PLAN record (and an LLD record for the issue-only and build-only routes) alongside the BUILD, so prepareReviewPacket and everything downstream is unchanged and the packet still lists story, lld and plan.
pros: No change to the review code at all
cons: Fabricates design and plan artifacts that the route deliberately did not have, which misrepresents the ledger and the process flow this Story must follow
Those records would need approval or be unapproved clutter, and every consumer of Plans (tracker, chain views) would see them
Moves the hardcoding into the build stage instead of removing it
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Falsifies the ledger to fit the validator, which is the opposite of following the process flow.

alternativesConsidered.name: Review the BUILD's tasks for every route
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Make the BUILD record the only required input and treat the design documents as optional context for all routes.
alternativesConsidered.approach: The review units are always the BUILD's tasks, with acceptance checks taken from the Plan task of the same id when a Plan exists and from the available design record otherwise. All three design documents become optional context, so the validation stops requiring a Plan for any route.
pros: One uniform unit source for every route, matching what the completion gate already compares
cons: Changes the unit for Plan-driven Stories as well, which the issue says must stay unchanged, and loses Plan-level size, order and planned tests in the assignment
A Story could drop its Plan from the packet and still pass, weakening the design-to-code check the review exists for
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Uniform and simple, but it changes Plan-driven reviews and lets a Story omit its Plan.

openQuestions: Which Story-definition document does a Plan-driven standalone Story pin as documents.story? Recommendation: the story role is required only when a DEF exists for the epicHash (an epic Story, where it is the DEF); a standalone Story has none, so its set is lld and plan, and the plan-path identity check uses the Plan artifact id.

Should the derived unit's size thresholds be fixed in the LLD? Recommendation: S for one or two changed files, M up to eight, L above, so the unit's timeout is 5, 10 or 15 minutes as the existing size table gives.
